summary: Possible typosquat of @solana/spl-token under unrelated scope
details: Package name `@solana-labs/spl-toke` resembles the legitimate Solana SPL Token client `@solana/spl-token` (note the missing trailing `n` in `spl-toke` and the use of the `@solana-labs` scope rather than `@solana`). The bundled output (`lib/index.cjs.js`, `lib/index.esm.js`) contains the typical co-occurrence of `require('child_process')`, `curl`, `ping`, `fetch(` and `POST` patterns inside a minified bundle, but tracing of the execution paths did not complete, so it is not confirmed whether these primitives are reachable at install/import time or are part of legitimate utilities bundled into the SDK. Given the strong name-confusion risk against a widely-used Solana ecosystem package, this should be reviewed by a human before allowing installs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
